blindSummary:
This state/province - the country's capital - recorded the highest transfeminicide toll of any state in 2024: 17 killings of LGBT+ people, 11 of them trans women, and remained among the highest-count states in 2025. The raw violence data is a negative signal for a visitor, though part of the elevated count reflects the capital's superior reporting infrastructure rather than proportionally higher danger.

Counterbalanced by an institutional response matched by no other state: transfeminicide became a distinct crime in July 2024 under a law named for a trans woman killed in 2016 (the second state to create the offence); a dedicated transfeminicide investigation unit covering all violent deaths of trans women was created inside the capital's attorney general's office in December 2024; a prosecutor's protocol issued in 2025 requires context-sensitive investigation with immediate-action deadlines (72h/48h); and a new gender-police unit with 30 patrol vehicles launched in August 2025. Legal gender recognition has existed here since 2014 and was opened to 12-year-olds by a 2021 decree. For a visitor assaulted in this state/province there is trained machinery to investigate; in several other large states there is none.

The protective and investigative framework is therefore the most extensive in the country, and materially changes what a visitor who encounters violence or discrimination faces after the fact, even though the recorded pre-violence risk data is the country's highest.
